name: MAURITIUS

flag.title: Les Quatre Bandes
flag.note: Four equal stripes: red, blue, yellow, green

lead: Mauritius is a tiny island in the Indian Ocean, 2,000 km off Africa. No one lived here until the 1600s. People came from Holland, France, Britain, Africa and India. It was the only home of the dodo.

facts.label: Top peak
facts.sub: Piton de la Petite Rivière Noire

geo: Mauritius is a volcanic island ringed by coral reefs and clear lagoons. Black sand beaches and basalt cliffs dot the coast.
The Seven Coloured Earths at Chamarel are dunes striped red, violet, blue and yellow. Iron in the volcanic soil makes the colours.
animals: In 1991 just 10 pink pigeons survived in the wild. Careful care has brought back hundreds. The Mauritian flying fox, a big fruit bat, pollinates the forest at night.
Spinner dolphins, green sea turtles and reef fish swim in the lagoons. Aldabra giant tortoises, up to 250 kg, were brought in to restore the island's nature.
culture: Mauritius is Africa's only Hindu-majority nation. People celebrate Eid, Christmas, Diwali and Chinese New Year. Try dholl puri, an Indian flatbread, or rougaille, a Creole stew.
Sega music began when enslaved Africans danced around campfires. UNESCO honoured it in 2014. Players beat goatskin drums called ravanne.
history: Dutch sailors reached uninhabited Mauritius in 1638. Their rats and pigs ate dodo eggs. By 1681 the dodo was gone forever.
France built sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans. Britain took the island in 1810 and freed them. Mauritius became independent peacefully on 12 March 1968 and a republic in 1992.
wows: The dodo went extinct in under 80 years after its first sighting.
From the air, the sea off the south-west looks like an underwater waterfall.
Mauritius has no indigenous people, because everyone descends from settlers.
The Seven Coloured Earths re-separate into bands, even after mixing.
Enslaved people created sega music, now UNESCO heritage.
Mauritius briefly became a high-income country in 2020.
The dodo on Mauritius's coat of arms has been extinct for over 340 years.

myths.fact: It is independent. Nearby Réunion is part of France.

myths.myth: The dodo was a made-up story
myths.fact: Dodos were real. Sailors drew them, and scientists have dug up their bones.
